profile.headline: Engineering @ Infinite Epigenetics | MS CS @ Georgia Tech | Reinforcement Learning, Backend Engineering
profile.summary:
I’m an experienced software engineer specializing in scalable, performant backend systems that process large-scale data and power machine learning–driven products. I am particularly excited by reinforcement learning and natural language processing.

I especially enjoy working with lean, early-stage startups, where I can bridge engineering and product, taking ideas quickly from concept through launch. I care about building intuitive, high-quality products that users genuinely enjoy using, so I'm comfortable working full-stack.

positions.title: Staff Software Engineer, Research and Platform
positions.description:
Infinite Epigenetics builds epigenetic diagnostic tests for healthcare providers, researchers, and consumers. Through TruDiagnostic, it serves a network of 7,500+ healthcare providers and collaborates with researchers at Harvard, Yale, and Duke.

Engineering lead for research, public API, Tally Health, and developer infrastructure.

positions.title: Senior Software Engineer
positions.description: Skills: C# · Python · TypeScript · Machine Learning · Deep Learning

positions.title: Senior Software Engineer
positions.description:
Scaling the bare metal instance API in Oracle Cloud Infrastructure’s Compute organization.

I worked on the scaling team, which focuses on scaling up the bare metal instance API for managing customer compute instances. I built asynchronous workflows to tombstone records after a certain period of time as part of an effort that cleaned up to 1TB of storage per region to enable our database team to scale more efficiently and support more customers. I also built a new API to improve performance when attaching and detaching VNICs to bare metal instances from 0.125 to 6 requests per second to meet our networking team's needs. OCI has also had explosive growth, so I have helped onboard new hires while we rapidly scale the Compute organization.

positions.title: Software Engineer
positions.description: Wild Health provides healthcare and guidance based on a patient's specific genetics. I worked on the Core team, where I led development for our genome processing engine and a greenfield LLM API to better answer patient questions based on their full health history. I built out models to classify a patient's sleep profile, gluten sensitivity, and dementia risk. I also implemented CI/CD pipelines to enable automated testing and deployments to Elastic Beanstalk and Kubernetes clusters, as well as maintained cloud resources on AWS, like ECR and EKS.
positions.insights: Skills: Celery · Redis · Kubernetes · Python · Django · FastAPI · PostgreSQL

positions.title: Co-Founder
positions.description: Skills: Machine Learning · Python · PyTorch · PostgreSQL · Amazon Web Services (AWS)

positions.title: Software Engineer
positions.description: Skills: SQL · Node.js · React.js · GraphQL · TypeScript · JavaScript

positions.title: Undergraduate Researcher
positions.description: I worked under Dr. Brent Seales at the Digital Restoration Initiative, where they work on very old, brittle manuscripts that cannot be physically opened out of fear they might be damaged and lost forever. They use their custom software pipeline to virtually unwrap and read these historical works without harming them.

positions.title: Undergraduate Researcher
positions.description: I worked under Dr. Michael Johnson in his Bioacoustics laboratory, where I cleaned datasets to enable mapping speech kinematics to pronunciation.

honors.title: First Place - Computer and Information Science Poster Presentation
honors.description: Undergraduate researchers presented two posters on our team's work at the Kentucky Academy of Science's 2019 Annual Meeting, where we took both first and second place.
honors.issuer: Issued by Kentucky Academy of Science · Nov 2019

honors.title: SMART Scholarship Program Participant
honors.description: The SMART (Science, Mathematics, and Research for Transformation) program was established by the Department of Defense to support undergraduates pursuing STEM degrees and increase the number of civilian scientists and engineers in DoD laboratories. The scholarship pays for schooling for X amount of years, and the recipient promises X years of service in return at their Sponsoring Facility. Acceptance rate is around 8 percent, varying from year to year.
